transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what really made me come in is... things at work are just not right. I'm a wholesale buyer, and lately, I just can't shake the feeling that people at work—and even some of our vendors—are tracking my buys. Like, they're secretly messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. My supervisor keeps pulling up the reports to show me they don't prove that, but I know what's happening. 

And honestly, the vendors are something else. There's this one guy I deal with, he always wears these ridiculously bright polo shirts. Neon orange, mostly. It reminds me of those traffic cones they used to put up near my old high school. They were doing all this construction on the main road for, like, three years straight when I was a teenager. I used to have to take this crazy detour through a neighborhood where this one guy had these little ceramic gnomes in his yard. Hundreds of them, just staring at the street. It was super weird, my buddy and I used to count them. But yeah... anyway, I just know they're altering my numbers.
Do you think these people at work and the vendors are actually out to get you, or is it just that you feel like something is off?

No, they are definitely out to get me. It's not just a feeling. I know they're tracking my buys. They're going into the system and messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. My supervisor keeps pulling up the reports, trying to show me that the numbers don't prove it, but I know what I'm seeing. 

And it's funny you mention feeling like something is off, because I was just at the grocery store the other day, and the cashier was looking at me exactly like my supervisor does. She had this little name tag that said "Brenda," but it was crooked. I almost told her to fix it, but then I remembered how my mom used to hate it when people pointed out stuff like that. She was always so particular about her clothes. She used to iron everything, even my jeans when I was in high school. I hated it. They always felt so stiff, you know? Like cardboard. I used to try and break them in by doing squats in my bedroom before the bus came. But yeah, the numbers... they're definitely altering them. I'm not crazy.
Do you feel like your thoughts are connected and make sense when you're talking about what's going on at work?

I mean, yeah, I think they make perfect sense. I know what I'm talking about when I say they're messing with my numbers. It's clear as day to me. But sometimes... I don't know, maybe I do get a little sidetracked. Like right now, I just remembered this one time I was trying to explain to my supervisor about the vendors, and I got totally distracted by this stain on his tie. It looked exactly like the shape of Florida. I went to Florida once when I was a kid. We drove all the way down to Orlando, and the AC in my dad's car broke halfway there. It was miserable. We had to roll all the windows down, and the wind was so loud we couldn't even hear the radio. My dad was playing this old cassette tape of the Eagles on repeat. I still can't listen to "Hotel California" without sweating. But anyway, yeah, I think my thoughts are connected. I just... I notice things, you know?
Do you often find it difficult to stay focused on one topic when talking about something important?

I don't know, I haven't really noticed that being a problem. I feel like I stay pretty focused on the important stuff. Like, when I'm looking at the purchase orders, I'm locked in. Though, they just switched the supplier for our printer paper at the office, and it's so thin now. It feels exactly like the tissue paper my grandma used to stuff inside my birthday cards. She always put a crisp five-dollar bill in there. Never ten, always five. I used to take that five bucks down to the corner store and buy those little wax bottles with the colored syrup inside. You know the ones? You bite the top off... they tasted like pure plastic, honestly, but my buddy and I loved them. The guy who ran the store had this huge handlebar mustache that curled all the way up his cheeks. 

But anyway... no, I don't really think I have a hard time staying on topic. I usually get my point across just fine.
Do you think your mind ever jumps between ideas in a way that doesn't make sense to other people?

I don't really think so. I mean, people seem to get what I'm saying just fine. I don't feel like my mind is jumping around or anything. Speaking of jumping, though, my cousin used to have this massive trampoline in his backyard. We'd go over there all the time when we were younger, and one summer I tried to do a double front flip and totally landed wrong. Snapped my arm right in half. They had to put pins in it and everything. The hospital food was the worst part, honestly. They gave me this green jello that tasted like... I don't know, dusty lime? My mom tried to sneak me in some fries from the drive-thru, but the head nurse caught her. That nurse had the loudest shoes, just squeaked every single time she walked down the linoleum hall. Squeak, squeak, squeak. Drove me crazy. 

But yeah, no, I don't think I confuse people when I talk. I make sense.
Do you think other people have trouble following your train of thought when you're explaining something?

I mean, no, not really. People usually just nod and agree with me, so I assume they're following along just fine. Like, just yesterday I was talking to the guy at the deli counter about the new vendor shipments we're dealing with at work, and he seemed totally on board. Speaking of the deli, they have this really good spicy mustard there now. It's got those little seeds in it? Reminds me of the mustard my uncle used to put on his hot dogs at the Fourth of July cookouts. He'd always burn the hot dogs, like, pitch black on the outside. We had to scrape the char off with a plastic knife. One time, my cousin accidentally swallowed a piece of the plastic knife because it snapped off in the meat. We had to take him to the emergency room, and we missed the fireworks. They were doing the big ones over the lake that year, too. You could hear the booms echoing off the water from miles away. It sounded like thunder. I love thunderstorms, honestly, the way the sky turns that weird purple color right before it pours. 

But yeah, no, I don't think people have trouble following me. They get it.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are disjointed or not flowing logically?

I don't think so. My thoughts feel perfectly logical to me, they just flow from one thing to the next like water. Which is funny, because our water pressure at my apartment has been terrible lately. I called the landlord about it, but he never answers his phone. He's this older guy, always wears these bright yellow suspenders. Reminds me of a fireman or something. Actually, I wanted to be a fireman when I was a little kid. I had this plastic red helmet I wore everywhere, even to the grocery store. My mom hated it because the strap would always dig into my chin and leave a red mark. She used to try and hide it in the hall closet, but I always found it behind the winter coats. The closet always smelled like mothballs and wet wool. 

But no, my thoughts aren't disjointed. They make perfect sense.
Have you ever heard or seen things that you know are not really there?

Well, sometimes, yeah. Like, if I'm in the stockroom at work, or driving back from a vendor meeting, I'll hear this man's voice. It sounds like he's right behind me, just saying, "Move faster, Scott," or he'll start laughing at the inventory picks I just made. And I'll turn around, and there's nobody there. It's really weird. Speaking of driving, though, my car has been making this awful rattling noise lately. It sounds like a bunch of loose change shaking around in a tin can. I think it might be the muffler, but I'm not a car guy. My dad was a car guy, though. He used to spend every weekend in the garage, covered in grease, working on this old Chevy Nova. He loved that car more than anything. He'd always listen to classic rock on this beat-up boombox while he worked. I can still hear the bass from that thing vibrating through the floorboards into the kitchen. My mom used to complain about the noise all the time, especially when she was trying to watch her soap operas. She never missed an episode of General Hospital. 

But yeah, I do hear that voice sometimes when nobody is around.
Do you think the voice you hear when you're alone is trying to tell you something specific?

I don't know if he's trying to tell me something specific, really. He just says things like, "Move faster, Scott," or he just laughs at me. Like he's judging the inventory picks I just made in the stockroom. It's always right behind me, too, like he's standing right over my shoulder. It happens when I'm driving back from vendor meetings, too. I hate those meetings, honestly. The vendors are always trying to push these new energy drinks on us. They come in these tall, skinny cans with neon green writing on them. They taste like battery acid, but people buy them like crazy. My buddy Dave drinks, like, three of them a day. I told him he's gonna give himself a heart attack, but he doesn't listen. Dave's stubborn like that. He once refused to wear a jacket in the middle of winter just to prove a point about cold tolerance. We were standing outside waiting for the bus, and it was snowing sideways. The snow was stinging my face like little needles. I hate the cold. It makes my joints ache, especially my knees. I messed up my knee playing basketball in high school. Landed wrong after a layup and just heard a pop. It swelled up to the size of a grapefruit. I had to wear this huge brace for months. It smelled terrible, like old sweat and neoprene. 

But yeah, the voice just tells me to move faster or laughs at me. I don't know what it means.
Do you feel like the voice you hear and the people altering your numbers at work are all part of the same thing happening to you?

I haven't really thought about it like that. I don't know if they're connected. The voice is just... there. And the numbers, well, that's someone messing with my spreadsheets. Spreadsheets are such a pain anyway. We use this ancient software at work, it looks like it's from the nineties. The background is this awful gray color, and the font is so tiny you have to squint to read it. I told my manager we need to upgrade, but he says it's not in the budget. He's always talking about the budget. He has this little bald spot right on the crown of his head, and whenever he gets stressed about money, he rubs it. It's actually kind of funny to watch. He reminds me of my middle school math teacher, Mr. Henderson. He used to sweat so much during tests, he'd have these huge pit stains on his shirts. He always smelled like old coffee and peppermint breath mints. He was a nice guy, though. He let me retake a test once when I completely bombed it because I stayed up all night playing video games. I used to be obsessed with this one racing game, I'd play it for hours until my thumbs went numb. 

So, I don't know if the voice and the numbers are part of the same thing. I haven't really noticed a connection.
Do you feel like your thoughts and actions are helping you achieve what you want to accomplish at work?

I mean, I guess? Sometimes I feel like I'm getting a massive amount done. Like, when I get really keyed up, I can't just sit there and handle one task. I'll be emailing three different vendors at the exact same time, making a whole new buy plan, and reorganizing all the product samples we have. I'll just be pacing the office the whole time, because I feel like if I stop moving, I'll completely lose the thread of what I'm doing. 

Pacing ruins my shoes, though. I bought these leather slip-ons a couple months ago and the soles are already wearing thin on the heels. I usually just buy cheap shoes anyway because I drag my feet. My mom used to yell at me for scuffing up the kitchen floor when I was a teenager. We had this awful linoleum that was supposed to look like brick, but it was just orange squares. It was always peeling up in the corners near the sink. The sink always leaked, too. It was just a slow drip, drip, drip all night. Drove me crazy. I tried to fix it once with some duct tape, but it just made the water spray sideways all over the counter. I had to use all my mom's good towels to mop it up. She was so mad she didn't talk to me for two days. She was very particular about her towels. They had to be folded in thirds, not in half. 

But yeah, when I'm keyed up at work, I just have to keep moving and doing a bunch of things at once.
Do you think your thoughts are organized when you're talking about multiple things at once?

I don't really know. I guess they make sense to me at the time. It's just that everything is happening so fast in my head, you know? Like, I'll be talking about the buy plan and then I'll remember the product samples, and it all feels connected right then. It's kind of like how a spider web works, all these little threads attaching to each other. I used to be terrified of spiders when I was a kid. My older brother, he used to catch these huge wolf spiders in the backyard and put them in my bed. He thought it was hilarious. He was always doing stuff like that, pulling pranks. Once he put Saran wrap over the toilet bowl. That was a disaster. My dad made him scrub the entire bathroom with a toothbrush after that. The bathroom always smelled like bleach anyway, because my dad was kind of a neat freak. He used to vacuum the living room every single day. The vacuum cleaner was this heavy, old Hoover that sounded like an airplane taking off. It drove our dog, Buster, absolutely insane. He'd bark at it and try to bite the wheels. Buster was a golden retriever mix, best dog ever. 

But anyway, yeah, I don't know if my thoughts are organized or not. They just come out however they come out.
Do you think your thoughts are disjointed when you're explaining something important to someone?

I don't know if they're disjointed, exactly. It's more like... people tell me I talk over them in meetings. Like, once I start explaining a new drop or a big deal I'm trying to work out, the words just come out so fast. I get going and I barely even notice anyone trying to jump in or ask a question. It's like I have to get it all out before I forget it. 

I actually got in trouble for that in high school once. We had this debate class, and I was supposed to be arguing about... I think it was school uniforms? Yeah, school uniforms. I was so against them. I mean, wearing the same thing every day is just so boring. I like wearing my vintage band tees. I have this really cool Nirvana shirt I found at a thrift store. It's perfectly faded and has this tiny hole near the collar, but that just makes it look better, you know? Thrift stores are the best. You never know what you're gonna find. I found a working Atari console once for like ten bucks. Best day ever. We hooked it up to this old tube TV my grandma gave me. The picture was always a little fuzzy, and you had to smack the side of the TV sometimes to fix the color, but playing Pac-Man on it was awesome. 

So yeah, I guess I just talk really fast when it's important, and people can't always get a word in edgewise.
Do you think your thoughts are disorganized when you're not talking about work or vendors?

I don't really know if they're disorganized outside of work. I haven't really thought about it, honestly. Like, when I'm just hanging out with my friends, we mostly just talk about music or whatever. Speaking of music, my buddy Dave just got this amazing new sound system for his car. It's ridiculous. The bass is so loud it actually makes your chest vibrate when you're sitting in the passenger seat. We were driving around the other night listening to this new techno mix he found, and it felt like we were in a club. 

Dave's car is this old Honda Civic that he's been fixing up for years. He painted it this really bright, obnoxious green color. He says it makes it go faster, which is stupid, but whatever. He's always working on it in his driveway. His driveway is gravel, though, which is terrible for working on cars. You drop a bolt in that stuff and it's just gone forever. I helped him change his oil once and I lost the little cap that goes on the tire valve. We spent like twenty minutes looking for it in the rocks. I hate gravel driveways. They're so noisy when you drive on them, too. It sounds like you're crushing bones or something. 

But yeah, I haven't really noticed if my thoughts are disorganized when I'm not at work. I guess I just talk like I always do.
Do you find your thoughts are disjointed when talking about things that have nothing to do with work?

I mean, I don't really think so. I guess I just talk the way I talk. Like, even if I'm just talking about, I don't know, what I had for lunch. I had this really good turkey sandwich today, actually. It was from that deli down the street, the one with the neon sign that's always buzzing. The buzzing drives me crazy if I stand in there too long. It sounds like a giant mosquito trapped in a jar. I got bit by a mosquito on my ankle yesterday and it itches so bad. I tried putting that pink lotion on it, calamine or whatever, but it smells weird. It smells like old chalk. We used to have chalkboards in elementary school and the teacher would make us clap the erasers outside. The dust would get everywhere, all over your clothes and in your hair. It looked like powdered sugar. I love powdered sugar donuts. The little mini ones that come in a bag. 

But anyway, no, I don't really notice if things get disjointed when I'm not talking about work. I just say what's on my mind.
Do you find that your thoughts jump around a lot when you're talking about things that have nothing to do with your job or the people you think are altering your numbers?

Not really. I don't feel like I'm jumping around at all. Speaking of jumping around, though, my little cousin had his birthday at one of those indoor trampoline parks last weekend. Have you ever been to one of those? It's literally just wall-to-wall trampolines. It sounds awesome until you actually get in there and realize the whole building smells like dirty socks. Like, intensely like feet. You have to buy these special grip socks with the little rubber dots on the bottom so you don't slip and break your neck. 

I got the neon orange ones. Orange was my favorite color when I was a kid, mostly because of Michelangelo from the Ninja Turtles. He was definitely the best one because he had the nunchucks and he was always eating pizza. I actually tried to make a homemade pizza from scratch yesterday, but the dough didn't rise right. It ended up flat like a cracker. A giant, burnt cheesy cracker. It still tasted okay with enough ranch on it, but it wasn't exactly what I was going for. 

So, no, I haven't noticed my thoughts doing that. I'm just having normal conversations.
Do you think the voice you hear is affecting how your thoughts are organized when you're talking about something important?

I mean, I don't know if it messes up my thoughts when I'm talking to people, because I mostly just hear it when I'm by myself. Like, sometimes when I'm in the stockroom or driving back from a vendor meeting, I'll hear this man's voice. It sounds like it's coming from right behind me, just saying, "Move faster, Scott," or he's laughing at my picks. And I'll turn around, and nobody's there. 

It really freaked me out the first time it happened in my car, because my car is tiny. It's this little hatchback I got a few years ago. The air conditioning in it is totally busted, so I have to drive with the windows down all summer. Driving with the windows down on the highway is the worst, though, because the wind just whips your hair right into your eyes. I need to get a haircut, actually. My barber, Tony, he's been cutting my hair since I was like ten. He always gives me a lollipop when I leave, even though I'm twenty-two. It's always the cherry ones. Cherry is okay, but blue raspberry is definitely the best flavor for candy. Jolly Ranchers, especially. I could eat a whole bag of blue raspberry Jolly Ranchers until my tongue turns completely blue. 

But yeah, I don't know if the voice makes my thoughts disorganized or anything.
Do you think the voice you hear affects how your thoughts are put together when you're talking about something important?

I mean, I don't really think it affects how I talk when it's important. Like I said, it mostly just happens when I'm alone, so I'm not really trying to have a serious conversation with anyone anyway. It's just me and the voice. And it's not like he's trying to have a conversation with me, he's just... commenting. 

Like, if I'm doing inventory, he'll just say something about how slow I am. Inventory is the absolute worst part of my job, by the way. You have to count every single box of these tiny little brass fittings, and they all look exactly the same. They come in these huge cardboard boxes that always smell like damp basement. My grandma's basement used to smell exactly like that. She had this old, green shag carpet down there that was probably from the seventies. We used to play board games on it. Monopoly was her favorite, but she always cheated. She would hide hundred-dollar bills under the board when nobody was looking. I caught her once, and she just laughed and gave me a butterscotch candy. I hate butterscotch. It tastes like old people. 

But no, I don't think the voice messes up my thoughts when I'm actually talking to someone about something important.
Do you find that your thoughts are disjointed or hard to follow when you're talking to friends or family about things that have nothing to do with work?

I don't think they're hard to follow. My friends and family haven't said anything about me being disjointed or whatever. I was just talking to my mom on the phone the other day, actually, and it was a totally normal conversation. We were mostly just talking about her dog, Buster. He's this huge Golden Retriever mix, and he keeps digging these massive holes all over her backyard. She was telling me how she tried putting cayenne pepper in the dirt to stop him, but he just sneezed a bunch and kept digging anyway. 

Speaking of pepper, I went to this new Thai place with my buddy Dave on Tuesday, and I asked for a level five spicy on my Pad Thai. Big mistake. My mouth was literally on fire for like an hour. We had to go get ice cream right after just to cool it down. I got mint chocolate chip. Mint chocolate chip is the best, but only if the ice cream is actually green, you know? If it's white, it just doesn't taste right for some reason. It's like a mental block or something. 

But yeah, I haven't noticed any issues with my thoughts when I'm just talking to people about regular stuff. Everything seems fine to me.
Do you find that your thoughts are hard to follow when talking to others in your daily life?

I feel like we kind of just went over this, but no, not really. I talk to people all day and it's totally fine. Like, I was just talking to the cashier at the grocery store last night, and we had a completely normal conversation. 

I was there buying cereal because I completely ran out of Cinnamon Toast Crunch. Cinnamon is actually kind of a crazy concept if you really think about it. It's literally just tree bark. Like, who was the first guy in history to look at a tree and say, "Hey, I'm gonna scrape the bark off that and put it on my oatmeal"? It had to be someone who was just starving, right? Or maybe they were chopping wood and some sawdust fell in their food. I tried building a birdhouse out of wood once in shop class back in high school. Mr. Henderson was the teacher. He was missing half of his left index finger from a table saw accident way back in the day. He used to point at us with the little stub when we were goofing off in the back of the room. It was hilarious but also kind of gross, honestly. 

But anyway, yeah, no, my thoughts are fine. People understand me just fine in my day-to-day life.
